chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with cutting the grey hair, and plucking it, and cutting it is more beloved to me than plucking it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pluck or cut grey hair according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of grooming grey hair (shamat), affirming the permissibility of both cutting (jaz) and plucking (natf). He explicitly states a preference for cutting, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that cutting is less likely to cause damage to the hair follicle compared to plucking. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader Islamic emphasis on cleanliness (taharah) and removing signs of aging to maintain a neat appearance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it, and cutting it is more beloved to me than plucking it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful to clip or pull out gray from the head but clipping is more likable to me.”
